tasks.help: The <c>dotnet test</c> command is used to execute unit tests in a given project. Unit tests are console application projects that have dependencies on the unit test framework (for example, MSTest, NUnit, or xUnit) and the dotnet test runner for the unit testing framework. These are packaged as NuGet packages and are restored as ordinary dependencies for the project.<para/>These are the options of the VSTest runner. When <c>global.json</c> selects Microsoft.Testing.Platform, use <c>DotNetTestMtp</c> instead.

properties.name: ProjectFile
properties.help: Specifies a path to the test project. If omitted, it defaults to current directory.

properties.name: TestAdapterPath
properties.help: Use the custom test adapters from the specified path in the test run.

properties.name: Configuration
properties.help: Configuration under which to build. The default value is <c>Debug</c>, but your project's configuration could override this default SDK setting.

properties.name: DataCollector
properties.help: Enables data collector for the test run. For more information, see Monitor and analyze test run.

properties.name: DiagnosticsFile
properties.help: Enables diagnostic mode for the test platform and write diagnostic messages to the specified file.

properties.name: Framework
properties.help: Looks for test binaries for a specific framework.

properties.name: Filter
properties.help: Filters out tests in the current project using the given expression. For more information, see the Filter option details section. For additional information and examples on how to use selective unit test filtering, see Running selective unit tests.

properties.name: Loggers
properties.help: Specifies a logger for test results. Specify the parameter multiple times to enable multiple loggers.

properties.name: NoBuild
properties.help: Does not build the test project prior to running it.

properties.name: NoRestore
properties.help: Doesn't perform an implicit restore when running the command.

properties.name: Output
properties.help: Directory in which to find the binaries to run.

properties.name: ResultsDirectory
properties.help: The directory where the test results are going to be placed. The specified directory will be created if it doesn't exist.

properties.name: SettingsFile
properties.help: Settings to use when running tests.

properties.name: ListTests
properties.help: List all of the discovered tests in the current project.

properties.name: Verbosity
properties.help: Sets the verbosity level of the command. Allowed values are <c>q[uiet]</c>, <c>m[inimal]</c>, <c>n[ormal]</c>, <c>d[etailed]</c>, and <c>diag[nostic]</c>.

properties.name: Properties
properties.help:
Set or override the specified project-level properties, where name is the property name and value is the property value. Specify each property separately, or use a semicolon or comma to separate multiple properties, as the following example shows:

/property:WarningLevel=2;OutDir=bin\Debug

properties.name: BlameMode
properties.help: Runs the tests in blame mode. This option is helpful in isolating the problematic tests causing test host to crash. It creates an output file in the current directory as Sequence.xml that captures the order of tests execution before the crash.

properties.name: BlameCrash
properties.help:
Runs the tests in blame mode and collects a crash dump when the test host exits unexpectedly. This option depends on the version of .NET used, the type of error, and the operating system.

For exceptions in managed code, a dump will be automatically collected on .NET 5.0 and later versions. It will generate a dump for testhost or any child process that also ran on .NET 5.0 and crashed. Crashes in native code will not generate a dump. This option works on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

Crash dumps in native code, or when using .NET Core 3.1 or earlier versions, can only be collected on Windows, by using Procdump. A directory that contains procdump.exe and procdump64.exe must be in the PATH or PROCDUMP_PATH environment variable. Download the tools. Implies --blame.

To collect a crash dump from a native application running on .NET 5.0 or later, the usage of Procdump can be forced by setting the VSTEST_DUMP_FORCEPROCDUMP environment variable to 1.

properties.name: BlameCrashDumpType
properties.help: The type of crash dump to be collected. Implies --blame-crash.

properties.name: BlameCrashCollectAlways
properties.help: Collects a crash dump on expected as well as unexpected test host exit.

properties.name: BlameHang
properties.help: Run the tests in blame mode and collects a hang dump when a test exceeds the given timeout.

properties.name: BlameHangDumpType
properties.help: The type of crash dump to be collected. It should be full, mini, or none. When none is specified, test host is terminated on timeout, but no dump is collected. Implies --blame-hang.

properties.name: BlameHangTimeout
properties.help:
Per-test timeout, after which a hang dump is triggered and the test host process and all of its child processes are dumped and terminated. The timeout value is specified in one of the following formats:

  • 1.5h, 1.5hour, 1.5hours
  • 90m, 90min, 90minute, 90minutes
  • 5400s, 5400sec, 5400second, 5400seconds
  • 5400000ms, 5400000mil, 5400000millisecond, 5400000milliseconds

When no unit is used (for example, 5400000), the value is assumed to be in milliseconds. When used together with data driven tests, the timeout behavior depends on the test adapter used. For xUnit and NUnit the timeout is renewed after every test case. For MSTest, the timeout is used for all test cases. This option is supported on Windows with netcoreapp2.1 and later, on Linux with netcoreapp3.1 and later, and on macOS with net5.0 or later. Implies --blame and --blame-hang.

properties.name: NoLogo
properties.help: Run test(s), without displaying Microsoft Testplatform banner. Available since .NET Core 3.0 SDK.

properties.name: ArtifactsPath
properties.help: All build output files from the executed command will go in subfolders under the specified path, separated by project. For more information see Artifacts Output Layout. Available since .NET 8 SDK.

tasks.help: Runs tests with Microsoft.Testing.Platform (MTP). This is the dotnet test of the .NET 10 SDK and later when global.json selects the platform: "test": { "runner": "Microsoft.Testing.Platform" }. Its options differ from the VSTest options of DotNetTest.Options for dotnet test itself come first. Options for the test applications come after a single --. An option of an extension works only when every test application references the extension's package. Otherwise the run fails with exit code 5. For more details, visit the official website.

properties.name: ProjectFile
properties.help: The test project to run, or a folder that contains it. Use only one of <c>ProjectFile</c>, <c>SolutionFile</c> and <c>TestModules</c>.

properties.name: SolutionFile
properties.help: The solution to run, or a folder that contains it. Use only one of <c>ProjectFile</c>, <c>SolutionFile</c> and <c>TestModules</c>.

properties.name: TestModules
properties.help: A glob of already built test applications to run, such as <c>**/bin/**/Release/net10.0/*.Tests.dll</c>. Use only one of <c>ProjectFile</c>, <c>SolutionFile</c> and <c>TestModules</c>. Can't be used with <c>Configuration</c>, <c>Framework</c>, <c>Runtime</c>, <c>Architecture</c> or <c>OperatingSystem</c>.

properties.name: TestModulesRootDirectory
properties.help: The root directory of the <c>TestModules</c> glob.

properties.name: MaxParallelTestModules
properties.help: The maximum number of test applications that run at the same time. The default is the number of processors.

properties.name: ConfigFile
properties.help: The testconfig.json file to use.

properties.name: Configuration
properties.help: The build configuration. The default for most projects is <c>Debug</c>.

properties.name: Framework
properties.help: The target framework to run the tests for. The project must target it.

properties.name: Runtime
properties.help: The runtime identifier to test for.

properties.name: Architecture
properties.help: The target architecture. It's combined with the default runtime identifier. Don't use it together with <c>Runtime</c>.

properties.name: OperatingSystem
properties.help: The target operating system. It's combined with the default runtime identifier. Don't use it together with <c>Runtime</c>.

properties.name: UseCurrentRuntime
properties.help: Uses the current runtime as the target runtime. Needs the .NET 11 SDK.

properties.name: ArtifactsPath
properties.help: Puts all build output in subfolders of this path, separated by project. For more information see Artifacts Output Layout. Needs the .NET 11 SDK.

properties.name: NoBuild
properties.help: Doesn't build the test projects before running them. Implies <c>NoRestore</c>.

properties.name: NoRestore
properties.help: Doesn't run an implicit restore.

properties.name: NoDependencies
properties.help: Doesn't build the project-to-project references. Needs the .NET 11 SDK.

properties.name: Verbosity
properties.help: The MSBuild verbosity level.

properties.name: Properties
properties.help: Sets or overrides MSBuild properties.

properties.name: EnvironmentVariables
properties.help: Sets environment variables for the test applications. These override the values of a launch profile.

properties.name: ResultsDirectory
properties.help: The directory for the test results. It's created when it doesn't exist.

properties.name: ResultsDirectoryLayout
properties.help: How a run of several test applications organizes the results directory. <c>flat</c> (the default) writes all results to one directory. <c>per-module</c> writes the results of each application to a subdirectory, so files with the same name don't overwrite each other. Needs the .NET SDK 10.0.402 or later.

properties.name: DiagnosticOutputDirectory
properties.help: The directory for the diagnostic output.

properties.name: MinimumExpectedTests
properties.help: The minimum number of tests of the whole run, including skipped tests. The run fails with exit code 9 when fewer tests run. For a minimum per test application, use <c>MinimumExpectedTestsPerModule</c>.

properties.name: MaximumFailedTests
properties.help: Stops the run after this number of failed tests, with exit code 13. Applies to the whole run with the .NET 11 SDK, and to each test application before.

properties.name: Timeout
properties.help: Stops the run after this time, such as <c>90s</c>, <c>10m</c> or <c>2h</c>, with exit code 3. Applies to the whole run with the .NET 11 SDK, and to each test application before.

properties.name: ListTests
properties.help: Lists the discovered tests instead of running them.

properties.name: NoAnsi
properties.help: Doesn't write ANSI escape characters to the screen.

properties.name: NoProgress
properties.help: Doesn't report progress to the screen.

properties.name: NoLogo
properties.help: Hides the .NET and Microsoft.Testing.Platform banners. Needs the .NET 11 SDK.

properties.name: NoArtifactPostProcessing
properties.help: Doesn't merge compatible reports, such as TRX files, after a run of several test applications. Needs the .NET 11 SDK.

properties.name: NoLaunchProfile
properties.help: Doesn't use <c>launchSettings.json</c> to configure the test applications.

properties.name: NoLaunchProfileArguments
properties.help: Doesn't use the <c>commandLineArgs</c> of the launch profile.

properties.name: OutputVerbosity
properties.help: The verbosity of the test output. <c>Minimal</c> needs Microsoft.Testing.Platform 2.4 or later.

properties.name: Filter
properties.help: Runs the tests that match the expression. The syntax belongs to the test framework. MSTest, NUnit and xunit.v3 take the VSTest filter syntax.

properties.name: TreenodeFilter
properties.help: Runs the tests that match the tree filter expression, for test frameworks that support it, such as TUnit.

properties.name: FilterUids
properties.help: Runs the tests with these test node UIDs.

properties.name: MinimumExpectedTestsPerModule
properties.help: The minimum number of tests of each test application. Skipped tests don't count. A test application fails with exit code 9 when fewer tests run.

properties.name: ZeroTestsPolicy
properties.help: Whether a test application that skipped all its tests fails. <c>allow-skipped</c> (the default) lets it pass. <c>strict</c> fails it with exit code 8. Needs Microsoft.Testing.Platform 2.3 or later.

properties.name: IgnoreExitCodes
properties.help: Exit codes of the test applications that count as success, such as 8 for a test application without tests. See the exit codes.

properties.name: Diagnostic
properties.help: Writes a diagnostic log for each test application.

properties.name: DiagnosticVerbosity
properties.help: The level of the diagnostic log. The default is <c>Trace</c>.

properties.name: DiagnosticFilePrefix
properties.help: The prefix of the diagnostic log file names.

properties.name: ReportTrx
properties.help: Writes a TRX report. Needs the <c>Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.TrxReport</c> package.

properties.name: ReportTrxFileName
properties.help: The file name of the TRX report, relative to the results directory. Needs <c>ReportTrx</c>.

properties.name: Coverage
properties.help: Collects code coverage. Needs the <c>Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.CodeCoverage</c> package.

properties.name: CoverageOutput
properties.help: The file name of the coverage report, relative to the results directory. Give each test application its own name, or the reports overwrite each other.

properties.name: CoverageOutputFormat
properties.help: The format of the coverage report. The default is <c>coverage</c>.

properties.name: CoverageSettings
properties.help: An XML file with code coverage settings.

properties.name: Coverlet
properties.help: Collects code coverage with Coverlet. Needs the <c>coverlet.MTP</c> package.

properties.name: CoverletOutputFormats
properties.help: The formats of the Coverlet reports. The default is <c>json</c> and <c>cobertura</c>.

properties.name: CoverletFilePrefix
properties.help: The prefix of the Coverlet report file names. Give each test application its own prefix, or the reports overwrite each other.

properties.name: CoverletIncludeFilters
properties.help: Includes the assemblies and types that match the filters, such as <c>[MyAssembly]MyNamespace.*</c>.

properties.name: CoverletExcludeFilters
properties.help: Excludes the assemblies and types that match the filters, such as <c>[*.Tests]*</c>.

properties.name: CoverletExcludeByFiles
properties.help: Excludes the source files that match the glob patterns, such as <c>**/*.Generated.cs</c>.

properties.name: CoverletExcludeByAttributes
properties.help: Excludes the methods and classes that have these attributes.

properties.name: CoverletIncludeTestAssembly
properties.help: Includes the test assembly in the coverage report.

properties.name: CoverletSingleHit
properties.help: Counts at most one hit for each location in the code.

properties.name: CoverletSkipAutoProps
properties.help: Skips auto-implemented properties.

properties.name: CoverletThreshold
properties.help: Fails the test application when the coverage percentage is lower.

properties.name: CrashDump
properties.help: Writes a dump file when a test application crashes. Needs the <c>Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.CrashDump</c> package.

properties.name: CrashDumpType
properties.help: The type of the crash dump. The default is <c>Full</c>.

properties.name: HangDump
properties.help: Writes a dump file and stops the test application when it runs longer than <c>HangDumpTimeout</c>. Needs the <c>Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.HangDump</c> package.

properties.name: HangDumpTimeout
properties.help: The time after which the hang dump is written, such as <c>90s</c> or <c>10m</c>. The default is <c>30m</c>.

properties.name: HangDumpType
properties.help: The type of the hang dump. The default is <c>Full</c>. <c>None</c> stops the test application without a dump.

properties.name: RetryFailedTests
properties.help: Runs failed tests again, at most this number of times. Needs the <c>Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.Retry</c> package.

properties.name: ReportGitHubActions
properties.help: Writes log groups, annotations and a job summary on GitHub Actions. Needs the <c>Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.GitHubActionsReport</c> package.

properties.name: ReportAzureDevOps
properties.help: Writes errors, warnings and annotations in the format of Azure Pipelines. Needs the <c>Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.AzureDevOpsReport</c> package.

properties.name: TestApplicationArguments
properties.help: Other arguments for the test applications, such as the options of the test framework (for example <c>--report-xunit-trx</c> of xunit.v3) or of other extensions.

tasks.help:
The dotnet run command provides a convenient option to run your application from the source code with one command. It's useful for fast iterative development from the command line. The command depends on the dotnet build command to build the code. Any requirements for the build, such as that the project must be restored first, apply to dotnet run as well.

Output files are written into the default location, which is bin/<configuration>/<target>. For example if you have a netcoreapp1.0 application and you run dotnet run, the output is placed in bin/Debug/netcoreapp1.0. Files are overwritten as needed. Temporary files are placed in the obj directory.

If the project specifies multiple frameworks, executing dotnet run results in an error unless the -f|--framework <FRAMEWORK> option is used to specify the framework.

The dotnet run command is used in the context of projects, not built assemblies. If you're trying to run a framework-dependent application DLL instead, you must use dotnet without a command. For example, to run myapp.dll, use: dotnet myapp.dll

For more information on the dotnet driver, see the .NET Core Command Line Tools (CLI) topic.

In order to run the application, the dotnet run command resolves the dependencies of the application that are outside of the shared runtime from the NuGet cache. Because it uses cached dependencies, it's not recommended to use dotnet run to run applications in production. Instead, create a deployment using the dotnet publish command and deploy the published output.

properties.name: Architecture
properties.help: Specifies the target architecture. This is a shorthand syntax for setting the Runtime Identifier (RID), where the provided value is combined with the default RID. For example, on a win-x64 machine, specifying --arch x86 sets the RID to win-x86. If you use this option, don't use the -r|--runtime option. Available since .NET 6 Preview 7.

properties.name: Configuration
properties.help: Configuration to use for building the project. The default value is Debug.

properties.name: DisableBuildServers
properties.help: Force the command to ignore any persistent build servers. This option provides a consistent way to disable all use of build caching, which forces a build from scratch. A build that doesn't rely on caches is useful when the caches might be corrupted or incorrect for some reason. Available since .NET 7 SDK.

properties.name: Framework
properties.help: Builds and runs the app using the specified framework. The framework must be specified in the project file.

properties.name: LaunchProfile
properties.help: The name of the launch profile (if any) to use when launching the application. Launch profiles are defined in the launchSettings.json file and are typically called Development, Staging and Production. For more information, see Working with multiple environments.

properties.name: Interactive
properties.help: Allows the command to stop and wait for user input or action. For example, to complete authentication. Available since .NET Core 3.0 SDK.

properties.name: NoBuild
properties.help: Doesn't build the project before running.

properties.name: NoLaunchProfile
properties.help: Doesn't attempt to use launchSettings.json to configure the application.

properties.name: NoRestore
properties.help: Doesn't perform an implicit restore when running the command.

properties.name: NoSelfContained
properties.help: Publish your application as a framework dependent application. A compatible .NET runtime must be installed on the target machine to run your application.

properties.name: OperatingSystem
properties.help: Specifies the target operating system (OS). This is a shorthand syntax for setting the Runtime Identifier (RID), where the provided value is combined with the default RID. For example, on a win-x64 machine, specifying --os linux sets the RID to linux-x64. If you use this option, don't use the -r|--runtime option. Available since .NET 6.

properties.name: ProjectFile
properties.help: Specifies the path and name of the project file. (See the NOTE.) It defaults to the current directory if not specified.

properties.name: Runtime
properties.help: Specifies the target runtime. For a list of Runtime Identifiers (RIDs), see the RID catalog.

properties.name: SelfContained
properties.help: Publishes the .NET runtime with the application so the runtime doesn't need to be installed on the target machine. The default is <c>false</c>. However, when targeting .NET 7 or lower, the default is <c>true</c> if a runtime identifier is specified.

properties.name: Verbosity
properties.help: Sets the verbosity level of the command. Allowed values are <c>q[uiet]</c>, <c>m[inimal]</c>, <c>n[ormal]</c>, <c>d[etailed]</c>, and <c>diag[nostic]</c>.

properties.name: ApplicationArguments
properties.help: Arguments passed to the application being run.

properties.name: ArtifactsPath
properties.help: All build output files from the executed command will go in subfolders under the specified path, separated by project. For more information see Artifacts Output Layout. Available since .NET 8 SDK.

tasks.help:
The dotnet restore command uses NuGet to restore dependencies as well as project-specific tools that are specified in the project file. By default, the restoration of dependencies and tools are performed in parallel.

Starting with .NET Core 2.0, you don't have to run dotnet restore because it's run implicitly by all commands, such as dotnet build and dotnet run, that require a restore to occur. It's still a valid command in certain scenarios where doing an explicit restore makes sense, such as continuous integration builds in Visual Studio Team Services or in build systems that need to explicitly control the time at which the restore occurs.

In order to restore the dependencies, NuGet needs the feeds where the packages are located. Feeds are usually provided via the NuGet.config configuration file. A default configuration file is provided when the CLI tools are installed. You specify additional feeds by creating your own NuGet.config file in the project directory. You also specify additional feeds per invocation at a command prompt.

For dependencies, you specify where the restored packages are placed during the restore operation using the --packages argument. If not specified, the default NuGet package cache is used, which is found in the .nuget/packages directory in the user's home directory on all operating systems (for example, /home/user1 on Linux or C:\Users\user1 on Windows).

For project-specific tooling, dotnet restore first restores the package in which the tool is packed, and then proceeds to restore the tool's dependencies as specified in its project file.

The behavior of the dotnet restore command is affected by some of the settings in the Nuget.Config file, if present. For example, setting the globalPackagesFolder in NuGet.Config places the restored NuGet packages in the specified folder. This is an alternative to specifying the --packages option on the dotnet restore command. For more information, see the NuGet.Config reference.

properties.name: ProjectFile
properties.help: Optional path to the project file to restore.

properties.name: ConfigFile
properties.help: The NuGet configuration file (NuGet.config) to use for the restore operation.

properties.name: Verbosity
properties.help: Sets the verbosity level of the command. Allowed values are <c>q[uiet]</c>, <c>m[inimal]</c>, <c>n[ormal]</c>, <c>d[etailed]</c>, and <c>diag[nostic]</c>.

properties.name: ArtifactsPath
properties.help: All build output files from the executed command will go in subfolders under the specified path, separated by project. For more information see Artifacts Output Layout. Available since .NET 8 SDK.

tasks.help:
The dotnet pack command builds the project and creates NuGet packages. The result of this command is a NuGet package. If the --include-symbols option is present, another package containing the debug symbols is created.

NuGet dependencies of the packed project are added to the .nuspec file, so they're properly resolved when the package is installed. Project-to-project references aren't packaged inside the project. Currently, you must have a package per project if you have project-to-project dependencies.

By default, dotnet pack builds the project first. If you wish to avoid this behavior, pass the --no-build option. This is often useful in Continuous Integration (CI) build scenarios where you know the code was previously built.

You can provide MSBuild properties to the dotnet pack command for the packing process. For more information, see NuGet metadata properties and the MSBuild Command-Line Reference.

properties.name: Project
properties.help: The project to pack. It's either a path to a csproj file or to a directory. If omitted, it defaults to the current directory.

properties.name: Configuration
properties.help: Configuration to use when building the project. If not specified, configuration defaults to <c>Debug</c>.

properties.name: IncludeSource
properties.help: Includes the source files in the NuGet package. The sources files are included in the <c>src</c> folder within the <c>nupkg</c>.

properties.name: IncludeSymbols
properties.help: Generates the symbols <c>nupkg</c>.

properties.name: NoBuild
properties.help: Don't build the project before packing.

properties.name: NoRestore
properties.help: Doesn't perform an implicit restore when running the command.

properties.name: OutputDirectory
properties.help: Places the built packages in the directory specified.

properties.name: Serviceable
properties.help: Sets the serviceable flag in the package. For more information, see .NET Blog: .NET 4.5.1 Supports Microsoft Security Updates for .NET NuGet Libraries.

properties.name: Verbosity
properties.help: Sets the verbosity level of the command. Allowed values are <c>q[uiet]</c>, <c>m[inimal]</c>, <c>n[ormal]</c>, <c>d[etailed]</c>, and <c>diag[nostic]</c>.

properties.name: VersionSuffix
properties.help: Defines the value for the <c>$(VersionSuffix)</c> MSBuild property in the project.

properties.name: NoLogo
properties.help: Doesn't display the startup banner or the copyright message. Available since .NET Core 3.0 SDK.

properties.name: ArtifactsPath
properties.help: All build output files from the executed command will go in subfolders under the specified path, separated by project. For more information see Artifacts Output Layout. Available since .NET 8 SDK.

properties.name: BinaryLog
properties.help: Generate MSBuild binary log.

tasks.help:
The dotnet build command builds the project and its dependencies into a set of binaries. The binaries include the project's code in Intermediate Language (IL) files with a .dll extension and symbol files used for debugging with a .pdb extension. A dependencies JSON file (*.deps.json) is produced that lists the dependencies of the application. A .runtimeconfig.json file is produced, which specifies the shared runtime and its version for the application.

If the project has third-party dependencies, such as libraries from NuGet, they're resolved from the NuGet cache and aren't available with the project's built output. With that in mind, the product of dotnet buildd isn't ready to be transferred to another machine to run. This is in contrast to the behavior of the .NET Framework in which building an executable project (an application) produces output that's runnable on any machine where the .NET Framework is installed. To have a similar experience with .NET Core, you use the dotnet publish command. For more information, see .NET Core Application Deployment.

Building requires the project.assets.json file, which lists the dependencies of your application. The file is created dotnet restore is executed. Without the assets file in place, the tooling cannot resolve reference assemblies, which will result in errors. With .NET Core 1.x SDK, you needed to explicitily run the dotnet restore before running dotnet build. Starting with .NET Core 2.0 SDK, dotnet restore runs implicitily when you run dotnet build. If you want to disable implicit restore when running the build command, you can pass the --no-restore option.

dotnet build uses MSBuild to build the project; thus, it supports both parallel and incremental builds. Refer to Incremental Builds for more information.

In addition to its options, the dotnet build command accepts MSBuild options, such as /p for setting properties or /l to define a logger. Learn more about these options in the MSBuild Command-Line Reference.

properties.name: ProjectFile
properties.help: The project file to build. If a project file is not specified, MSBuild searches the current working directory for a file that has a file extension that ends in proj and uses that file.

properties.name: Configuration
properties.help: Defines the build configuration. If omitted, the build configuration defaults to <c>Debug</c>. Use <c>Release</c> build a Release configuration.

properties.name: Framework
properties.help: Compiles for a specific framework. The framework must be defined in the project file.

properties.name: NoIncremental
properties.help: Marks the build as unsafe for incremental build. This turns off incremental compilation and forces a clean rebuild of the project's dependency graph.

properties.name: NoRestore
properties.help: Doesn't perform an implicit restore during build.

properties.name: OutputDirectory
properties.help: Directory in which to place the built binaries. You also need to define <c>--framework</c> when you specify this option.

properties.name: SelfContained
properties.help: Publishes the .NET runtime with the application so the runtime doesn't need to be installed on the target machine. The default is <c>true</c> if a runtime identifier is specified. Available since .NET 6 SDK

properties.name: Runtime
properties.help: Specifies the target runtime. For a list of Runtime Identifiers (RIDs), see the RID catalog.

properties.name: Verbosity
properties.help: Sets the verbosity level of the command. Allowed values are <c>q[uiet]</c>, <c>m[inimal]</c>, <c>n[ormal]</c>, <c>d[etailed]</c>, and <c>diag[nostic]</c>.

properties.name: VersionSuffix
properties.help: Defines the version suffix for an asterisk (<c>*</c>) in the version field of the project file. The format follows NuGet's version guidelines.

properties.name: Loggers
properties.help: Specifies the loggers to use to log events from MSBuild.

properties.name: NoConsoleLogger
properties.help: Disable the default console logger, and don't log events to the console.

properties.name: NoLogo
properties.help: Doesn't display the startup banner or the copyright message. Available since .NET Core 3.0 SDK.

properties.name: BinaryLog
properties.help: Generate MSBuild binary log.

properties.name: ArtifactsPath
properties.help: All build output files from the executed command will go in subfolders under the specified path, separated by project. For more information see Artifacts Output Layout. Available since .NET 8 SDK.

tasks.help: The dotnet msbuild command allows access to a fully functional MSBuild.The command has the exact same capabilities as the existing MSBuild command-line client for SDK-style projects only. The options are all the same. For more information about the available options, see the MSBuild command-line reference.The dotnet build command is equivalent to dotnet msbuild -restore. When you don't want to build the project and you have a specific target you want to run, use dotnet build or dotnet msbuild and specify the target.

properties.name: TargetPath
properties.help: The solution or project file on which MSBuild is executed.

properties.name: DetailedSummary
properties.help: Show detailed information at the end of the build log about the configurations that were built and how they were scheduled to nodes.

properties.name: MaxCpuCount
properties.help:
Specifies the maximum number of concurrent processes to use when building. If you don't include this switch, the default value is 1. If you include this switch without specifying a value, MSBuild will use up to the number of processors in the computer. For more information, see Building Multiple Projects in Parallel.

The following example instructs MSBuild to build using three MSBuild processes, which allows three projects to build at the same time:

msbuild myproject.proj /maxcpucount:3

properties.name: NodeReuse
properties.help:
Enable or disable the re-use of MSBuild nodes. You can specify the following values:

  • true: Nodes remain after the build finishes so that subsequent builds can use them (default).
  • false. Nodes don't remain after the build completes.

A node corresponds to a project that's executing. If you include the /maxcpucount switch, multiple nodes can execute concurrently.

properties.name: NoLogo
properties.help: Don't display the startup banner or the copyright message.

properties.name: Restore
properties.help: Runs the <c>Restore</c> target prior to building the actual targets.

properties.name: Targets
properties.help:
Build the specified targets in the project. Specify each target separately, or use a semicolon or comma to separate multiple targets, as the following example shows:
/target:Resources;Compile

If you specify any targets by using this switch, they are run instead of any targets in the DefaultTargets attribute in the project file. For more information, see Target Build Order and How to: Specify Which Target to Build First.

A target is a group of tasks. For more information, see Targets.

properties.name: Verbosity
properties.help:
Specifies the amount of information to display in the build log. Each logger displays events based on the verbosity level that you set for that logger.

You can specify the following verbosity levels: q[uiet], m[inimal], n[ormal], d[etailed], and diag[nostic].

The following setting is an example: /verbosity:quiet

properties.name: Loggers
properties.help: Specifies the loggers to use to log events from MSBuild.

properties.name: NoConsoleLogger
properties.help: Disable the default console logger, and don't log events to the console.

properties.name: Configuration
properties.help: Defines the build configuration. The default value is <c>Debug</c>. This option is only required when cleaning if you specified it during build time.

properties.name: GraphBuild
properties.help: Causes MSBuild to construct and build a project graph. Constructing a graph involves identifying project references to form dependencies. Building that graph involves attempting to build project references prior to the projects that reference them, differing from traditional MSBuild scheduling. Requires MSBuild 16 or later.

properties.name: BinaryLog
properties.help: Generate MSBuild binary log.

properties.name: Properties
properties.help:
Set or override the specified project-level properties, where name is the property name and value is the property value. Specify each property separately, or use a semicolon or comma to separate multiple properties, as the following example shows:

/property:WarningLevel=2;OutDir=bin\Debug

delegates.name: PublishReadyToRun
delegates.help: Compiles application assemblies as ReadyToRun (R2R) format. R2R is a form of ahead-of-time (AOT) compilation. For more information, see ReadyToRun images. Available since .NET Core 3.0 SDK.We recommend that you specify this option in a publish profile rather than on the command line. For more information, see MSBuild.

delegates.name: PublishSingleFile
delegates.help: Packages the app into a platform-specific single-file executable. The executable is self-extracting and contains all dependencies (including native) that are required to run the app. When the app is first run, the application is extracted to a directory based on the app name and build identifier. Startup is faster when the application is run again. The application doesn't need to extract itself a second time unless a new version is used. Available since .NET Core 3.0 SDK. For more information about single-file publishing, see the single-file bundler design document.We recommend that you specify this option in a publish profile rather than on the command line. For more information, see MSBuild.

delegates.name: PublishTrimmed
delegates.help: Trims unused libraries to reduce the deployment size of an app when publishing a self-contained executable. For more information, see Trim self-contained deployments and executables. Available since .NET Core 3.0 SDK as a preview feature.We recommend that you specify this option in a publish profile rather than on the command line. For more information, see MSBuild.

tasks.help: The dotnet clean command cleans the output of the previous build. It's implemented as an MSBuild target, so the project is evaluated when the command is run. Only the outputs created during the build are cleaned. Both intermediate (obj) and final output (bin) folders are cleaned.

properties.name: Project
properties.help: The MSBuild project to clean. If a project file is not specified, MSBuild searches the current working directory for a file that has a file extension that ends in proj and uses that file.

properties.name: Configuration
properties.help: Defines the build configuration. The default value is <c>Debug</c>. This option is only required when cleaning if you specified it during build time.

properties.name: Framework
properties.help: The framework that was specified at build time. The framework must be defined in the project file. If you specified the framework at build time, you must specify the framework when cleaning.

properties.name: Output
properties.help: Directory in which the build outputs are placed. Specify the <c>--framework</c> switch with the output directory switch if you specified the framework when the project was built.

properties.name: Runtime
properties.help: Cleans the output folder of the specified runtime. This is used when a self-contained deployment was created.

properties.name: Verbosity
properties.help: Sets the verbosity level of the command. Allowed levels are q[uiet], m[inimal], n[ormal], d[etailed], and diag[nostic].

properties.name: NoLogo
properties.help: Doesn't display the startup banner or the copyright message. Available since .NET Core 3.0 SDK.

properties.name: ArtifactsPath
properties.help: All build output files from the executed command will go in subfolders under the specified path, separated by project. For more information see Artifacts Output Layout. Available since .NET 8 SDK.

tasks.help: dotnet format is a code formatter that applies style preferences to a project or solution. Preferences will be read from an *.editorconfig* file, if present, otherwise a default set of preferences will be used. For more information, see the EditorConfig documentation

properties.name: Project
properties.help: The MSBuild project or solution to run code formatting on. If a project or solution file is not specified, MSBuild searches the current working directory for a file that has a file extension that ends in proj or sln, and uses that file.

properties.name: Severity
properties.help: The minimum severity of diagnostics to fix. Allowed values are info, warn, and error. The default value is warn.

properties.name: NoRestore
properties.help: Doesn't execute an implicit restore before formatting. Default is to do implicit restore.

properties.name: VerifyNoChanges
properties.help: Verifies that no formatting changes would be performed. Terminates with a non zero exit code if any files would have been formatted.

properties.name: Include
properties.help: A space-separated list of relative file or folder paths to include in formatting. The default is all files in the solution or project.

properties.name: Exclude
properties.help: A space-separated list of relative file or folder paths to exclude from formatting. The default is none.

properties.name: IncludeGenerated
properties.help: Formats files generated by the SDK.

properties.name: Verbosity
properties.help: Sets the verbosity level. Allowed levels are q[uiet], m[inimal], n[ormal], d[etailed], and diag[nostic].

properties.name: BinaryLog
properties.help: Logs all project or solution load information to a binary log file.

properties.name: Report
properties.help: Produces a JSON report in the directory specified by <c>REPORT_PATH</c>.

tasks.help:
dotnet publish compiles the application, reads through its dependencies specified in the project file, and publishes the resulting set of files to a directory. The output will contain the following:
  • Intermediate Language (IL) code in an assembly with a dll extension.
  • .deps.json file that contains all of the dependencies of the project.
  • .runtime.config.json file that specifies the shared runtime that the application expects, as well as other configuration options for the runtime (for example, garbage collection type).
  • The application's dependencies. These are copied from the NuGet cache into the output folder.
The dotnet publish command's output is ready for deployment to a hosting system (for example, a server, PC, Mac, laptop) for execution and is the only officially supported way to prepare the application for deployment. Depending on the type of deployment that the project specifies, the hosting system may or may not have the .NET Core shared runtime installed on it. For more information, see .NET Core Application Deployment. For the directory structure of a published application, see Directory structure.

properties.name: Project
properties.help: The project to publish, which defaults to the current directory if not specified.

properties.name: Architecture
properties.help: Specifies the target architecture. This is a shorthand syntax for setting the Runtime Identifier (RID), where the provided value is combined with the default RID. For example, on a win-x64 machine, specifying --arch x86 sets the RID to win-x86. If you use this option, don't use the -r|--runtime option. Available since .NET 6 Preview 7.

properties.name: Configuration
properties.help: Defines the build configuration. The default value is <c>Debug</c>.

properties.name: Framework
properties.help: Publishes the application for the specified target framework. You must specify the target framework in the project file.

properties.name: Manifest
properties.help: Specifies one or several target manifests to use to trim the set of packages published with the app. The manifest file is part of the output of the dotnet store command. To specify multiple manifests, add a --manifest option for each manifest. This option is available starting with .NET Core 2.0 SDK.

properties.name: NoRestore
properties.help: Doesn't perform an implicit restore when running the command.

properties.name: NoBuild
properties.help: Doesn't build the project before publishing. It also implicitly sets the <c>--no-restore</c> flag.

properties.name: Output
properties.help: Specifies the path for the output directory. If not specified, it defaults to ./bin/[configuration]/[framework]/ for a framework-dependent deployment or ./bin/[configuration]/[framework]/[runtime] for a self-contained deployment.If a relative path is provided, the output directory generated is relative to the project file location, not to the current working directory.

properties.name: OperatingSystem
properties.help: Specifies the target operating system (OS). This is a shorthand syntax for setting the Runtime Identifier (RID), where the provided value is combined with the default RID. For example, on a win-x64 machine, specifying --os linux sets the RID to linux-x64. If you use this option, don't use the -r|--runtime option. Available since .NET 6.

properties.name: SelfContained
properties.help: Publishes the .NET Core runtime with your application so the runtime doesn't need to be installed on the target machine. If a runtime identifier is specified, its default value is true. For more information about the different deployment types, see .NET Core application deployment.

properties.name: Runtime
properties.help: Publishes the application for a given runtime. This is used when creating a self-contained deployment (SCD). For a list of Runtime Identifiers (RIDs), see the RID catalog. Default is to publish a framework-dependent deployment (FDD).

properties.name: Verbosity
properties.help: Sets the verbosity level of the command. Allowed values are <c>q[uiet]</c>, <c>m[inimal]</c>, <c>n[ormal]</c>, <c>d[etailed]</c>, and <c>diag[nostic]</c>.

properties.name: VersionSuffix
properties.help: Defines the version suffix for an asterisk (<c>*</c>) in the version field of the project file. The format follows NuGet's version guidelines.

properties.name: NoLogo
properties.help: Doesn't display the startup banner or the copyright message. Available since .NET Core 3.0 SDK.

properties.name: Targets
properties.help:
Build the specified targets in the project. Specify each target separately, or use a semicolon or comma to separate multiple targets, as the following example shows:
/target:Resources;Compile

If you specify any targets by using this switch, they are run instead of any targets in the DefaultTargets attribute in the project file. For more information, see Target Build Order and How to: Specify Which Target to Build First.

A target is a group of tasks. For more information, see Targets.

properties.name: ArtifactsPath
properties.help: All build output files from the executed command will go in subfolders under the specified path, separated by project. For more information see Artifacts Output Layout. Available since .NET 8 SDK.

tasks.help: Pushes a package to the server and publishes it.

properties.name: TargetPath
properties.help: Path of the package to push.

properties.name: Source
properties.help: Specifies the server URL. This option is required unless <c>DefaultPushSource</c> config value is set in the NuGet config file.

properties.name: SymbolSource
properties.help: Specifies the symbol server URL.

properties.name: Timeout
properties.help: Specifies the timeout for pushing to a server in seconds. Defaults to 300 seconds (5 minutes). Specifying 0 (zero seconds) applies the default value.

properties.name: ApiKey
properties.help: The API key for the server.

properties.name: SymbolApiKey
properties.help: The API key for the symbol server.

properties.name: DisableBuffering
properties.help: Disables buffering when pushing to an HTTP(S) server to decrease memory usage.

properties.name: NoSymbols
properties.help: Doesn't push symbols (even if present).

properties.name: ForceEnglishOutput
properties.help: Forces all logged output in English.

properties.name: SkipDuplicate
properties.help: When pushing multiple packages to an HTTP(S) server, treats any 409 Conflict response as a warning so that the push can continue. Available since .NET Core 3.1 SDK.

properties.name: NoServiceEndpoint
properties.help: Doesn't append <c>api/v2/package</c> to the source URL. Option available since .NET Core 2.1 SDK.

tasks.help: The dotnet nuget delete command deletes or unlists a package from the server. For nuget.org, the action is to unlist the package.

properties.name: PackageId
properties.help: Package Id to delete. The exact behavior depends on the source. For local folders, for instance, the package is deleted; for nuget.org the package is unlisted.

properties.name: PackageVersion
properties.help: Package Version to delete. The exact behavior depends on the source. For local folders, for instance, the package is deleted; for nuget.org the package is unlisted.

properties.name: Source
properties.help: Specifies the server URL. This option is required unless <c>DefaultPushSource</c> config value is set in the NuGet config file.

properties.name: ApiKey
properties.help: The API key for the server.

properties.name: ForceEnglishOutput
properties.help: Forces all logged output in English.

properties.name: NoServiceEndpoint
properties.help: Doesn't append <c>api/v2/package</c> to the source URL. Option available since .NET Core 2.1 SDK.

properties.name: Interactive
properties.help: Allows the command to stop and wait for user input or action. For example, to complete authentication. Available since .NET Core 3.0 SDK.

properties.name: NonInteractive
properties.help: Doesn't prompt for user input or confirmations.

tasks.help: The dotnet nuget sign command signs all the packages matching the first argument with a certificate. The certificate with the private key can be obtained from a file or from a certificate installed in a certificate store by providing a subject name or a SHA-1 fingerprint.

properties.name: TargetPath
properties.help: Path of the package to sign.

properties.name: CertificatePath
properties.help: Specifies the file path to the certificate to be used in signing the package.

properties.name: CertificateStoreName
properties.help: Specifies the name of the X.509 certificate store to use to search for the certificate. Defaults to 'My', the X.509 certificate store for personal certificates. This option should be used when specifying the certificate via --certificate-subject-name or --certificate-fingerprint options.

properties.name: CertificateStoreLocation
properties.help: Specifies the name of the X.509 certificate store use to search for the certificate. Defaults to 'CurrentUser', the X.509 certificate store used by the current user. This option should be used when specifying the certificate via --certificate-subject-name or --certificate-fingerprint options.

properties.name: CertificateSubjectName
properties.help: Specifies the subject name of the certificate used to search a local certificate store for the certificate. The search is a case-insensitive string comparison using the supplied value, which finds all certificates with the subject name containing that string, regardless of other subject values. The certificate store can be specified by --certificate-store-name and --certificate-store-location options.

properties.name: CertificateFingerprint
properties.help: Specifies the fingerprint of the certificate used to search a local certificate store for the certificate. Starting with .NET 9, this option can be used to specify the SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384, or SHA-512 fingerprint of the certificate. However, a NU3043 warning is raised when a SHA-1 certificate fingerprint is used because it is no longer considered secure.

properties.name: CertificatePassword
properties.help: Specifies the certificate password, if needed. If a certificate is password protected but no password is provided, the sign command will fail.

properties.name: HashAlgorithm
properties.help: Hash algorithm to be used to sign the package. Defaults to SHA256. Possible values are SHA256, SHA384, and SHA512.

properties.name: Output
properties.help: Specifies the directory where the signed package should be saved. If this option isn't specified, by default the original package is overwritten by the signed package.

properties.name: Overwrite
properties.help: Indicate that the current signature should be overwritten. By default the command will fail if the package already has a signature.

properties.name: TimestampHashAlgorithm
properties.help: Hash algorithm to be used by the RFC 3161 timestamp server. Defaults to SHA256.

properties.name: Timestamper
properties.help: URL to an RFC 3161 timestamping server.

properties.name: Verbosity
properties.help: Sets the verbosity level of the command. Allowed values are <c>q[uiet]</c>, <c>m[inimal]</c>, <c>n[ormal]</c>, <c>d[etailed]</c>, and <c>diag[nostic]</c>.

tasks.help: The dotnet nuget verify command verifies a signed NuGet package.

properties.name: TargetPath
properties.help: Path of the package to verify.

properties.name: CertificateFingerprint
properties.help: Verify that the signer certificate matches with one of the specified SHA256 fingerprints. This option can be supplied multiple times to provide multiple fingerprints.

properties.name: ConfigFile
properties.help: The NuGet configuration file (nuget.config) to use.

properties.name: Verbosity
properties.help: Sets the verbosity level of the command. Allowed values are <c>q[uiet]</c>, <c>m[inimal]</c>, <c>n[ormal]</c>, <c>d[etailed]</c>, and <c>diag[nostic]</c>.

tasks.help: Adds a NuGet source.

properties.name: Source
properties.help: URL of the source.

properties.name: Name
properties.help: Name of the source.

properties.name: Username
properties.help: Username to be used when connecting to an authenticated source.

properties.name: Password
properties.help: Password to be used when connecting to an authenticated source.

properties.name: StorePasswordInClearText
properties.help: Enables storing portable package source credentials by disabling password encryption.

properties.name: ValidAuthenticationTypes
properties.help: List of valid authentication types for this source. Set this to <c>basic</c> if the server advertises NTLM or Negotiate and your credentials must be sent using the Basic mechanism, for instance when using a PAT with on-premises Azure DevOps Server. Other valid values include <c>negotiate</c>, <c>kerberos</c>, <c>ntlm</c>, and <c>digest</c>, but these values are unlikely to be useful.

properties.name: ConfigFile
properties.help: The NuGet configuration file (nuget.config) to use. If specified, only the settings from this file will be used. If not specified, the hierarchy of configuration files from the current directory will be used. For more information, see Common NuGet Configurations.

tasks.help: Updates a NuGet source.

properties.name: Name
properties.help: Name of the source.

properties.name: Source
properties.help: URL of the source.

properties.name: Username
properties.help: Username to be used when connecting to an authenticated source.

properties.name: Password
properties.help: Password to be used when connecting to an authenticated source.

properties.name: StorePasswordInClearText
properties.help: Enables storing portable package source credentials by disabling password encryption.

properties.name: ValidAuthenticationTypes
properties.help: List of valid authentication types for this source. Set this to <c>basic</c> if the server advertises NTLM or Negotiate and your credentials must be sent using the Basic mechanism, for instance when using a PAT with on-premises Azure DevOps Server. Other valid values include <c>negotiate</c>, <c>kerberos</c>, <c>ntlm</c>, and <c>digest</c>, but these values are unlikely to be useful.

properties.name: ConfigFile
properties.help: The NuGet configuration file (nuget.config) to use. If specified, only the settings from this file will be used. If not specified, the hierarchy of configuration files from the current directory will be used. For more information, see Common NuGet Configurations.

tasks.help:
The dotnet tool install command provides a way for you to install .NET Core Global Tools on your machine. To use the command, you either have to specify that you want a user-wide installation using the --global option or you specify a path to install it using the --tool-path option.Global Tools are installed in the following directories by default when you specify the -g (or --global) option:
  • Linux/macOS: $HOME/.dotnet/tools
  • Windows: %USERPROFILE%\.dotnet\tools

properties.name: PackageName
properties.help: The Name/ID of the NuGet package that contains the .NET Core Global Tool to install.

properties.name: Sources
properties.help: Adds an additional NuGet package source to use during installation.

properties.name: ConfigFile
properties.help: Specifies the NuGet configuration (nuget.config) file to use.

properties.name: Framework
properties.help: Specifies the target framework to install the tool for. By default, the .NET Core SDK tries to choose the most appropriate target framework.

properties.name: Global
properties.help: Specifies that the installation is user wide. Can't be combined with the <c>--tool-path</c> option. If you don't specify this option, you must specify the <c>--tool-path</c> option.

properties.name: ToolInstallationPath
properties.help: Specifies the location where to install the Global Tool. The path can be absolute or relative. If the path doesn't exist, the command tries to create it. Can't be combined with the <c>--global</c> option. If you don't specify this option, you must specify the <c>--global</c> option.

properties.name: Verbosity
properties.help: Sets the verbosity level of the command. Allowed values are <c>q[uiet]</c>, <c>m[inimal]</c>, <c>n[ormal]</c>, <c>d[etailed]</c>, and <c>diag[nostic]</c>.

properties.name: Version
properties.help: The version of the tool to install. By default, the latest stable package version is installed. Use this option to install preview or older versions of the tool.

tasks.help: The <c>dotnet tool restore</c> command finds the tool manifest file that is in scope for the current directory and installs the tools that are listed in it.

properties.name: ConfigFile
properties.help: Specifies the NuGet configuration (nuget.config) file to use.

properties.name: Sources
properties.help: Adds an additional NuGet package source to use during installation.

properties.name: ToolManifest
properties.help: Path to the manifest file.

properties.name: DisableParallel
properties.help: Prevent restoring multiple projects in parallel.

properties.name: IgnoreFailedSources
properties.help: Treat package source failures as warnings.

properties.name: NoCache
properties.help: Do not cache packages and http requests.

properties.name: Interactive
properties.help: Allows the command to stop and wait for user input or action (for example to complete authentication).

tasks.help: The <c>dotnet tool uninstall</c> command provides a way for you to uninstall .NET Core Global Tools from your machine. To use the command, you either have to specify that you want to remove a user-wide tool using the <c>--global</c> option or specify a path to where the tool is installed using the <c>--tool-path</c> option.

properties.name: PackageName
properties.help: The Name/ID of the NuGet package that contains the .NET Core Global Tool to uninstall. You can find the package name using the dotnet tool list command.

properties.name: Global
properties.help: Specifies that the tool to be removed is from a user-wide installation. Can't be combined with the <c>--tool-path</c> option. If you don't specify this option, you must specify the <c>--tool-path</c> option.

properties.name: ToolInstallationPath
properties.help: Specifies the location where to uninstall the Global Tool. The path can be absolute or relative. Can't be combined with the <c>--global</c> option. If you don't specify this option, you must specify the <c>--global</c> option.

properties.name: Verbosity
properties.help: Sets the verbosity level of the command. Allowed values are <c>q[uiet]</c>, <c>m[inimal]</c>, <c>n[ormal]</c>, <c>d[etailed]</c>, and <c>diag[nostic]</c>.

tasks.help: The <c>dotnet tool update</c> command provides a way for you to update .NET Core Global Tools on your machine to the latest stable version of the package. The command uninstalls and re-installs a tool, effectively updating it. To use the command, you either have to specify that you want to update a tool from a user-wide installation using the <c>--global</c> option or specify a path to where the tool is installed using the <c>--tool-path</c> option.

properties.name: PackageName
properties.help: The Name/ID of the NuGet package that contains the .NET Core Global Tool to install.

properties.name: Sources
properties.help: Adds an additional NuGet package source to use during installation.

properties.name: ConfigFile
properties.help: Specifies the NuGet configuration (nuget.config) file to use.

properties.name: Framework
properties.help: Specifies the target framework to update the tool for.

properties.name: Global
properties.help: Specifies that the installation is user wide. Can't be combined with the <c>--tool-path</c> option. If you don't specify this option, you must specify the <c>--tool-path</c> option.

properties.name: ToolInstallationPath
properties.help: Specifies the location where the Global Tool is installed. The path can be absolute or relative. Can't be combined with the <c>--global</c> option. If you don't specify this option, you must specify the <c>--global</c> option.

properties.name: Verbosity
properties.help: Sets the verbosity level of the command. Allowed values are <c>q[uiet]</c>, <c>m[inimal]</c>, <c>n[ormal]</c>, <c>d[etailed]</c>, and <c>diag[nostic]</c>.

properties.name: Version
properties.help: The version of the tool to install. By default, the latest stable package version is installed. Use this option to install preview or older versions of the tool.

tasks.help: The <c>dotnet workload install</c> command installs one or more optional workloads. Optional workloads can be installed on top of the .NET SDK to provide support for various application types, such as .NET MAUI and Blazor WebAssembly AOT.

properties.name: WorkloadId
properties.help: The workload ID or multiple IDs to install.

properties.name: ConfigFile
properties.help: The NuGet configuration file (nuget.config) to use. If specified, only the settings from this file will be used. If not specified, the hierarchy of configuration files from the current directory will be used.

properties.name: DisableParallel
properties.help: Prevents restoring multiple projects in parallel.

properties.name: IgnoreFailedSources
properties.help: Treats package source failures as warnings.

properties.name: IncludePreviews
properties.help: Allows prerelease workload manifests.

properties.name: Interactive
properties.help: Allows the command to stop and wait for user input or action. For example, to complete authentication.

properties.name: NoCache
properties.help: Prevents caching of packages and http requests.

properties.name: SkipManifestUpdate
properties.help: Skip updating the workload manifests. The workload manifests define what assets and versions need to be installed for each workload.

properties.name: SkipSignCheck
properties.help: Skipping the nuget package signature verification.

properties.name: Source
properties.help: Specifies the URI of the NuGet package source to use. This setting overrides all of the sources specified in the nuget.config files. Multiple sources can be provided by specifying this option multiple times.

properties.name: TempDir
properties.help: Specify the temporary directory used to download and extract NuGet packages (must be secure).

properties.name: Verbosity
properties.help: Sets the verbosity level of the command. Allowed values are <c>q[uiet]</c>, <c>m[inimal]</c>, <c>n[ormal]</c>, <c>d[etailed]</c>, and <c>diag[nostic]</c>.

tasks.help: The <c>dotnet workload uninstall</c> command uninstalls one or more workloads.

properties.name: WorkloadId
properties.help: The workload ID or multiple IDs to install.

tasks.help: The <c>dotnet workload restore</c> command analyzes a project or solution to determine which workloads it needs, then installs any workloads that are missing.

properties.name: Project
properties.help: The project or solution file to install workloads for. If a file is not specified, the command searches the current directory for one.

properties.name: ConfigFile
properties.help: The NuGet configuration file (nuget.config) to use. If specified, only the settings from this file will be used. If not specified, the hierarchy of configuration files from the current directory will be used.

properties.name: DisableParallel
properties.help: Prevents restoring multiple projects in parallel.

properties.name: IgnoreFailedSources
properties.help: Treats package source failures as warnings.

properties.name: IncludePreviews
properties.help: Allows prerelease workload manifests.

properties.name: Interactive
properties.help: Allows the command to stop and wait for user input or action. For example, to complete authentication.

properties.name: NoCache
properties.help: Prevents caching of packages and http requests.

properties.name: SkipManifestUpdate
properties.help: Skip updating the workload manifests. The workload manifests define what assets and versions need to be installed for each workload.

properties.name: SkipSignCheck
properties.help: Skipping the nuget package signature verification.

properties.name: Source
properties.help: Specifies the URI of the NuGet package source to use. This setting overrides all of the sources specified in the nuget.config files. Multiple sources can be provided by specifying this option multiple times.

properties.name: TempDir
properties.help: Specify the temporary directory used to download and extract NuGet packages (must be secure).

properties.name: Verbosity
properties.help: Sets the verbosity level of the command. Allowed values are <c>q[uiet]</c>, <c>m[inimal]</c>, <c>n[ormal]</c>, <c>d[etailed]</c>, and <c>diag[nostic]</c>.

tasks.help: The <c>dotnet workload update</c> command updates all installed workloads to the newest available versions. It queries Nuget.org for updated workload manifests. It then updates local manifests, downloads new versions of the installed workloads, and removes all old versions of each workload.

properties.name: AdvertisingManifestsOnly

commonTaskProperties.name: Properties
commonTaskProperties.help:
Set or override the specified project-level properties, where name is the property name and value is the property value. Specify each property separately, or use a semicolon or comma to separate multiple properties, as the following example shows:

--property:WarningLevel=2;OutDir=bin\Debug

delegates.name: PublishReadyToRun
delegates.help: Compiles application assemblies as ReadyToRun (R2R) format. R2R is a form of ahead-of-time (AOT) compilation. For more information, see ReadyToRun images. Available since .NET Core 3.0 SDK.We recommend that you specify this option in a publish profile rather than on the command line. For more information, see MSBuild.

delegates.name: PublishSingleFile
delegates.help: Packages the app into a platform-specific single-file executable. The executable is self-extracting and contains all dependencies (including native) that are required to run the app. When the app is first run, the application is extracted to a directory based on the app name and build identifier. Startup is faster when the application is run again. The application doesn't need to extract itself a second time unless a new version is used. Available since .NET Core 3.0 SDK. For more information about single-file publishing, see the single-file bundler design document.We recommend that you specify this option in a publish profile rather than on the command line. For more information, see MSBuild.

delegates.name: PublishTrimmed
delegates.help: Trims unused libraries to reduce the deployment size of an app when publishing a self-contained executable. For more information, see Trim self-contained deployments and executables. Available since .NET Core 3.0 SDK as a preview feature.We recommend that you specify this option in a publish profile rather than on the command line. For more information, see MSBuild.

restore.name: DisableParallel
restore.help: Disables restoring multiple projects in parallel.

restore.name: Force
restore.help: Forces all dependencies to be resolved even if the last restore was successful. This is equivalent to deleting the project.assets.json file.

restore.name: IgnoreFailedSources
restore.help: Only warn about failed sources if there are packages meeting the version requirement.

restore.name: NoCache
restore.help: Specifies to not cache packages and HTTP requests.

restore.name: NoDependencies
restore.help: When restoring a project with project-to-project (P2P) references, restore the root project and not the references.

restore.name: PackageDirectory
restore.help: Specifies the directory for restored packages.

restore.name: Sources
restore.help: Specifies a NuGet package source to use during the restore operation. This overrides all of the sources specified in the NuGet.config file(s). Multiple sources can be provided by specifying this option multiple times.

restore.name: UseLockFile
restore.help: Enables project lock file to be generated and used with restore.

restore.name: LockedMode
restore.help: Don't allow updating project lock file.

restore.name: LockFilePath
restore.help: Output location where project lock file is written. By default, this is 'PROJECT_ROOT\packages.lock.json'.

restore.name: ForceEvaluate
restore.help: Forces restore to reevaluate all dependencies even if a lock file already exists.

restore-runtime.name: Runtime
restore-runtime.help: Specifies a runtime for the package restore. This is used to restore packages for runtimes not explicitly listed in the <RuntimeIdentifiers> tag in the .csproj file. For a list of Runtime Identifiers (RIDs), see the RID catalog. Provide multiple RIDs by specifying this option multiple times.
